messages:
alex: Heads up — we have a customer reporting a bunch of 502s and intermittent "connection reset by peer" errors. Go SDK v0.12.3, custom http.Client + context timeouts. Anyone seen this pattern?

priya: Can you drop the minimal repro + logs here? Is this consistently after a context cancel / timeout?

alex: Logs show repeated retries from the SDK then connection resets. Root request has ctx timeout ~2s and we do a burst of parallel requests. Snippet of what their client looks like:

alex: ```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  MaxIdleConns: 100,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 10,
  IdleConnTimeout: 30 * time.Second,
  DisableKeepAlives: true, // they set this to true
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
req = req.WithContext(ctx)
resp, err := client.Do(req)
```

jamie: Two red flags: DisableKeepAlives=true and short IdleConnTimeout. If keep-alives are disabled the transport won't reuse sockets — you'll see more handshakes and more surface area for resets. Also ensure you don't reuse a canceled context for subsequent requests.

morgan: Also note older SDK retry logic (v0.12.3) will retry on 5xx and some transport errors. If the request body isn't rewindable (no GetBody) retries can behave oddly. We had a bug where the SDK attempted retries but the underlying transport had closed connections, leading to resets.

priya: If the body is non-nil you need a rewindable body for retries. Quick workaround: buffer the payload and use io.NopCloser(bytes.NewReader(buf)) so each retry gets a fresh ReadCloser. Or provide req.GetBody so net/http can re-read.

oncall: Concrete mitigations to try quickly:
- set DisableKeepAlives: false
- increase IdleConnTimeout to something >= retry window (e.g., 60s)
- set MaxIdleConnsPerHost to a higher number (50) for high concurrency
- add Transport.ResponseHeaderTimeout to avoid hung handshakes
- avoid using the same canceled context for a new request
- if using short per-request context deadlines, make client.Timeout > context deadline by a small margin to avoid double-cancel races

jamie: Example recommended transport:```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  MaxIdleConns: 200,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 50,
  IdleConnTimeout: 60 * time.Second,
  DisableKeepAlives: false,
  ResponseHeaderTimeout: 5 * time.Second,
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr, Timeout: 10 * time.Second}
```

alex: Good, we'll try that. Any SDK patches?

morgan: There's a patch in v0.12.5 that tweaks retry heuristics and fixes a body-reuse bug. Recommend upgrading the Go SDK to v0.12.5+; the changelog mentions "fix: retry with non-rewindable bodies and avoid reusing canceled contexts".

priya: Repro steps we gave the customer to validate: 1) run a small Go program that issues 200 parallel requests with ctx timeout=2s and body from bytes.Reader (not rewindable) against a test endpoint that randomly returns 502, 2) toggling DisableKeepAlives=true reproduces spikes, 3) upgrade SDK or switch to rewindable body removes the pattern.

alex: Test results: after flipping DisableKeepAlives=false and increasing IdleConnTimeout we saw 80% drop in connection resets. Planning SDK upgrade tomorrow. Thanks all :thumbsup:

support-bot: Ticket #CUST-4432 updated: engineer assigned -> alex. ETA for next update: 2026-03-18 16:00 UTC

oncall: If they still see problems after upgrade ping me and we'll remote debug.

jamie: Also add a short note in docs / troubleshooting about context cancel vs client.Timeout and retries — a lot of folks trip over this.

alex: Will add a snippet to the KB after we confirm.
